description: Farshid Dehghan publishes notebooks and workflows for building-performance prediction using EnergyPlus-derived data and machine learning. The June 2026 Zenodo archive is free under CC BY 4.0; the current GitHub repository exposes no separate licence. Its README describes a 79.35-square-metre dwelling in Sari, Iran, a present-climate set of 1,826 configurations, and future-weather experiments for 2050 and 2080 using HadCM3 and SRES A2. Regression, transfer-learning and disaggregation of prediction errors can support surrogate-building simulations and comparison of adaptation-data needs. Outputs include energy, carbon emissions, indoor-air-quality and comfort measures. Related catalogue record model-energyplus is the underlying simulator. The README describes several evolving experiments with different feature sets, so their designs must not be assumed interchangeable. Archive completeness, claimed calibration against utility data and uncertainty calculations were not independently checked. Generalisation beyond this building and climate pathway remains uncertain.
